title: A voice note that never mentions the step gets a clarifying ask; a real one counts
origin: Spec #7 (photo and voice verification): Watch item, a voice note about something else

history.text: Day 3 tonight, Maya. Ten pages of Atomic Habits at 8, then a quick voice note saying what you read.

plan.proof_note: a quick voice note saying what you read
plan.reason: Ten pages a night finishes the book this month.

testerLines: [voice: Ugh today was so long. Work was nonstop and then I made pasta for my roommates and we watched a movie.]
oh lol yeah I read my pages earlier
[voice: Okay, ten pages done. Chapter three, the part about identity-based habits, how you vote for who you want to be.]
whatWentWrong: New case, not a past mistake: a voice note that doesn't mention the step isn't proof, and their word alone isn't either.
shouldHaveHappened: The first voice note never mentions reading: ZOH responds warmly to their day but notes it didn't hear anything about the pages and asks naturally for the reading note. "I read my pages earlier" alone isn't proof: ZOH stays light and asks for the quick voice note saying what they read. The second voice note names the pages and chapter: ZOH celebrates and counts it, maybe referencing what they read (identity-based habits), without inventing anything.
